operativeStateAssessment.operativeDocument: doc-c (Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, dated April 21, 2026)
operativeStateAssessment.reasoning: Doc-c's own recitals state that Riot and Coinbase Credit "have agreed to amend and restate the Existing Credit Agreement with effect from the Second Amendment and Restatement Effective Date," where "Existing Credit Agreement" is defined as doc-b (the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated May 19, 2025, itself in the form it took after restating doc-a, which doc-c separately defines as the "Original Credit Agreement"). New Section 1.05 ("Amendment and Restatement"), which has no counterpart in doc-a or doc-b, states in operative terms that "[u]pon the effectiveness of this Agreement, the terms and provisions of the Existing Credit Agreement shall be superseded hereby" and that "[a]ll references to the Credit Agreement or any similar term contained in the Loan Documents shall be deemed to refer to this Agreement." Doc-c is signed (Jason Chung for Riot as CFO; Matthew Boyd for Coinbase Credit as Head of Prime Finance) and dated April 21, 2026, matching its own defined "Second Amendment and Restatement Effective Date" trigger mechanics in Section 3.04, which is itself gated on customary closing conditions including delivery of the Second Security Confirmation and (newly) a requirement that no Blocking Event be continuing. Taken together, doc-c's recitals, its Section 1.05 supersession language, and its execution/dating establish it as the document intended to be currently controlling as of the April 21, 2026 date in question, fully superseding doc-b (which itself had fully superseded doc-a per doc-b's own recitals and Section 3.03). The chain of supersession is therefore doc-a -> doc-b -> doc-c, with doc-c current and operative, and the underlying indebtedness treated as continuous (no novation) throughout.
